# Phase Two — Critique

The Awtsmoos does not confuse simplicity with deletion. We preserve every controller ID and every reachable capability while changing only when it is revealed.

## Risks and constraints
1. Preserve all existing IDs used by presenters/controllers.
2. Preserve all twelve routes.
3. Do not remove capability access; collapse it.
4. Do not break desktop layout while simplifying mobile.
5. Do not duplicate Create on Home.
6. Keep touch targets at least 44px for standalone controls.
7. Use semantic `<details>/<summary>` for disclosure when possible.
8. Avoid custom JS state if native disclosure can own it.
9. Preserve alias/destination/privacy text for context presenters.
10. Keep Home stats in DOM so HomePulse continues to update them.
11. Keep quick-action IDs in DOM so QuickActions remains functional.
12. Keep `pulseOrb`/`pulseTarget` IDs if controller code expects them, but mobile may visually compress the hero.
13. Keep persistent creator route contract, but alter presentation by route/mobile CSS.
14. Avoid a new monolithic stylesheet; split mobile-simple rules into focused modules.
15. Keep every touched source <=120 lines.
16. Full-file rewrites only.
17. Tabs in JS/CSS.
18. Required B"H/Awtsmoos/Awtsmoos.com comments remain.
19. Verify actual browser screenshots at mobile width after implementation.
20. Run existing route-quality and creator contracts so simplification cannot silently break behavior.

Simplicity is Gevurah: the Awtsmoos hides infinite depth behind the exact boundary the user needs now.
